Definition: from G1722 and G4154; to inhale, i.e. (figuratively) to be animated by (bent upon):--breathe.
BiblicalUsage: Saul was yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples in Acts 9:1 — his very breath was set against the church, and he carried letters to Damascus to hunt them down.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the man who breathed out murder became the man who breathed out the gospel, and no one's breath is too poisoned for God to change.
